operations.summary: Approves a pending authentication session. Supply the session's `authId` to identify the request you want to approve. The response confirms the operation with an empty object.

Registers a node through the authentication flow. Use `authId` to associate the registration with an authentication session and `user` to specify the user for the node. The response contains the registered node.
Rejects a pending authentication session. Supply the session's `authId` to identify the request you want to reject. The response confirms the operation with an empty object.
Backfills IP addresses for registered nodes. Use the `confirmed` query parameter to indicate whether to confirm the operation, and review the returned `changes` list to see what was updated.
Validates a policy against the server's live users and nodes without saving it. Provide `policy` as a string when included; the request body is required.
operations.description: Validates the given policy against the server's live users and nodes without persisting it.

operations.summary: Creates a new API key. You can provide `expiration` as a date-time value or omit it if you do not want to specify an expiration. The response contains the generated key in `apiKey`.

Creates a pre-auth key for a user. Configure the key with fields such as `user`, `expiration`, `reusable`, `ephemeral`, and `aclTags`; `user` is a uint64-formatted string and `expiration` is a date-time.
Creates a user record. You can provide `name`, `displayName`, `email`, and `pictureUrl`; all defined fields are strings and none is marked as required.

Creates a node for debugging purposes. Provide `name` and `user` to describe the node, and use `key` or `routes` when those values are needed for the test setup. The response contains the created node.
Deletes an API key selected by its prefix. You can also supply `id` as a uint64-formatted string to further identify the key. The response confirms the operation with an empty object.
Deletes a node identified by its ID. Supply `nodeId` as an unsigned 64-bit integer value to identify the node to remove.
Deletes a pre-auth key. Use the optional `id` query parameter to identify the key to delete; provide it as a uint64-formatted string when supplied.
Deletes a user by identifier. Provide the user's `id` as a uint64-formatted string in the path.
Expires an API key. Identify the key using `id`, `prefix`, or both, according to the key details available to you. The response confirms the operation with an empty object.
Updates the expiry settings for a node. Supply `expiry` as an ISO 8601 date-time or use `disableExpiry` to specify whether expiry is disabled.
Expires a pre-auth key. Supply its identifier in the `id` field as a uint64-formatted string when specifying which key to expire.
Retrieves a node by its identifier. Supply `nodeId` as an unsigned 64-bit integer value to identify the node.
Retrieves the current policy. The response includes the policy text and the time it was last updated.
Reports the server's health, including database connectivity. Read `databaseConnectivity` to determine whether the database connection is available.
operations.description: Reports server health, including database connectivity.

operations.summary: Lists the API keys available to the authenticated user. Review each key's identifier, prefix, expiration, creation time, and last-seen time to manage existing credentials.
Lists nodes managed by the service. Supply `user` to filter the results to nodes associated with that user; omit it to list nodes without a user filter.
Lists the pre-auth keys configured on the server. Use this operation to retrieve each key's user, key value, expiration, usage state, and ACL tags.
Lists users, with optional filters for user identifier, name, or email. Supply `id` as a uint64-formatted string when filtering by identifier; `name` and `email` are string filters.
Registers a node and returns its node record. Use `user` to associate the node with a user and `key` to provide a registration key when needed.
Renames a node by setting its new name. Supply the node identifier and the new name in the path.
Renames a user by changing the name associated with the specified identifier. Provide `oldId` as a uint64-formatted string and `newName` as a string in the path.
Updates the approved routes for a node. Send the route values in the `routes` array to set which routes are approved for that node.
Replaces the current policy with the policy value supplied in the request body. Include the policy text in `policy`; the response provides the saved policy and its update time.
Sets the tags for a node. Send the tags as an array of strings in the request body.
